questions.question: What is the primary focus of system integration testing?
options: C) Interactions among assembled modules or systems
questions.explanation: SIT checks that individually tested parts work together.

questions.question: Why can integration defects remain after all modules pass unit tests?
options: A) Modules can disagree about interface contracts
B) Unit tests prove every system property
questions.explanation: Formats, units, timing, and error handling can differ across boundaries.

questions.question: Which is a common module-interface mechanism listed in the slides?
questions.explanation: Procedure calls, shared memory, and message passing are the three listed paradigms.

questions.question: Integrating cart, inventory, and order modules inside one shop is what level?
questions.explanation: The modules belong to the same system.

questions.question: Connecting an e-commerce application to an independent payment system is what level?
questions.explanation: It joins separately tested systems across a system boundary.

questions.question: What does pairwise integration test?
options: B) Two interconnected systems at a time
C) Every possible pair of input values
D) All paths through every module
questions.explanation: The term here refers to connected systems, not combinatorial input generation.

questions.question: In this lecture, what is a build?
options: C) An interim compiled software image for internal testing
D) Only the final user manual
questions.explanation: Builds support incremental assembly and internal validation.

questions.question: After adding a module, what testing should accompany its new-interface tests?
options: A) Only a new logo check
B) Relevant regression tests on previously working behavior
C) No tests if compilation succeeded
questions.explanation: New interactions can disturb existing functionality.

questions.question: Which information belongs in a build release note?
options: A) Changes, fixed defects, and outstanding defects
B) Only the language's syntax rules
C) Only the final retail price
D) Only a list of tester birthdays
questions.explanation: Release notes make the build's scope and known state visible.

questions.question: Why retain prior daily builds?
options: A) To replace all interface specifications
B) To make every test infeasible
questions.explanation: A previously known build can help diagnose changes or recover from a broken increment.

questions.question: Which approach typically needs stubs for missing lower-level modules?
questions.explanation: High-level real callers need replacements for unavailable dependencies.

questions.question: Which approach typically needs drivers for missing callers?
questions.explanation: Drivers invoke real low-level modules or clusters.

questions.question: A real checkout service calls a fake tax dependency. What role does the fake dependency play?
questions.explanation: It replaces a called service, regardless of its class name.

questions.question: A harness invokes a real parser while its controller is unavailable. What role does the harness play?
questions.explanation: It supplies the missing caller role.

questions.question: What limitation is associated with bottom-up integration?
options: A) It guarantees complete system behavior immediately
C) Low-level modules cannot be tested
D) High-level design faults may be discovered late
questions.explanation: Top-level control/design arrives later.

questions.question: What characterizes big-bang integration?
options: A) Only test the bottom utilities with drivers
B) Always add one module per day
C) Only test the top module with stubs
D) Assemble the individually tested modules together and test the whole
questions.explanation: Many simultaneous interfaces can make defect localization harder.

questions.question: What middle-layer technique is used in the lecture's sandwich description?
options: B) Big-bang after top and bottom integration
questions.explanation: The lecture mixes top-down, bottom-up, and a middle joining stage.

questions.question: A class named PaymentGatewayDriver is called by the service under test and returns fake payment results. How should its role be interpreted?
options: A) Its name proves it is the caller driver
B) It is the real external gateway
C) It acts as a callee stub/test double despite its name
questions.explanation: Classify by the direction of calls, not an inconsistent name in an example.

questions.question: When are hardware DVT activities performed in the lecture's process?
options: B) Before integration with the software system
C) Never if a software build exists
questions.explanation: The hardware group prepares and executes design verification before software integration.

questions.question: What does a hardware/software compatibility matrix record?
questions.explanation: Compatibility can depend on both hardware and software revisions.

questions.question: What does ECO stand for in the slides?
questions.explanation: It formally describes a hardware/software change and includes compatibility information.

questions.question: Which is an SIT entry-readiness item in the sample framework?
options: A) Two weeks of final SIT uptime already completed
B) No modules remain to integrate
C) Approved specifications and completed passing unit testing
D) All final SIT results documented
questions.explanation: Entry criteria establish readiness to begin the integration phase.

questions.question: Which belongs to SIT exit rather than entry?
options: A) Choosing the initial hardware prototype only
B) All modules integrated and results documented
D) Creating a check-in form for the first time
questions.explanation: Exit criteria demonstrate completion of the defined phase.

questions.question: How many outstanding minor defects does the slide's example exit framework allow at most?
questions.explanation: This is the sample criterion on p. 31, not a universal release rule.

questions.question: Which SIT category targets the complete workflow across the integrated system?
questions.explanation: End-to-end validity checks the assembled workflow from start to finish.

questions.question: Keeping an integrated system running for weeks primarily fits which SIT category?
questions.explanation: The duration tests continued operation of the integrated system.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a wrapper around an OTS component?
options: B) Isolate or simplify the component interface
questions.explanation: It adapts the boundary around an underlying component.

questions.question: What does tailoring mean in this lecture?
options: B) Only rename a test case
D) Add behavior around a component without modifying its source
questions.explanation: Tailoring enriches the component's functionality through additions.

questions.question: Why deliberately inject a fault into a COTS component during system testing?
options: A) Observe system tolerance, error handling, and recovery
B) Avoid testing the integrated system
C) Replace every valid input with random noise permanently
D) Prove that the component can never fail
questions.explanation: Fault injection probes behavior when the component fails.

questions.question: In which built-in-testing mode can a user invoke internal tests and receive their summary?
questions.explanation: Normal operation hides the testing capability; maintenance exposes it for testing.
